items.title: China’s AI hardware push is moving beyond GPUs to the PCBs underneath them — Beijing races to corner the market on copper foil and micro-drill bits as board complexity explodes
items.description: AI hardware bottlenecks are expanding beyond GPUs to the PCBs underneath them. As AI servers like Rubin Ultra push PCB layers toward 78 layers using denser laminates, drill bits are wearing out 10 times faster than normal, while high-speed signalling stretches the demand for smooth copper foil.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Much of the attention on China's AI hardware industry has been focused on the country’s drive to develop domestic GPUs, including Huawei's Ascend processors, as U.S. export restrictions make it harder to buy advanced chips in the region. But making an AI server involves far more than securing its processors. The printed circuit boards (PCBs) connecting chips, memory, and networking equipment are becoming harder to manufacture, and Chinese companies are racing to supply the materials and equipment they require.More than 20 Chinese PCB manufacturers announced major expansion plans in the first half of 2026. Three recent reports from HSBC and J.P. Morgan suggest the shortages could extend to products as unglamorous as drill bits and copper foil. Having a plentiful and regular supply of those components in the manufacturing process is important because the tiny drill bit used to make the circuit boards inside AI servers could be worn out after drilling fewer than 200 holes, according to HSBC, compared with around 2,000 holes for older materials.It’s all part of a manufacturing process which stresses every part of the supply and manufacturing chain, beyond obvious components.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: More holes, fewer usesPCBs are built by layering copper and insulating material together, then drilling holes through them to connect their circuits. But the complexity of those boards is increasing as AI servers are designed to handle more data, including more layers than those seen in ordinary computers. HSBC estimates that a notebook PCB has four to eight layers, compared with more than 20 for Nvidia's H100 generation of GPUs.But that’s just the beginning of the process. Analysts at the bank forecast that a backplane in Nvidia’s Rubin Ultra systems could contain 78 layers. Nor is the Rubin Ultra an outlier in that process: the bank also forecasts a 36% annual rise in the number of holes required per board between 2025 and 2028. The holes themselves are becoming more challenging to drill. According to a report by Taiwanese brokerage KGI Securities, the ratio between the depth of the hole and its diameter has increased from around 20:1 to 30:1 or 40:1. That requires pushing an extremely thin drill bit deeper into increasingly tough materials without bending or breaking it, or damaging the delicate circuitry, which can easily happen in such a sophisticated manufacturing process. You may like AI demand triggers massive PCB shortage for PC makers as order books full until 2030 AI component hikes force the world's largest PC makers to return manufacturing capacity to China Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia GPUs in a single year, report claims As well as the number of layers which have to be drilled through increasing in number, the materials involved are also adding complexity to the equation. New grades of copper-clad laminate — the glass-fibre-and-resin material onto which copper is bonded — are becoming trickier for the tiny tungsten-carbide tools previously used in the process to cut. “AI PCBs are denser with thicker layers, requiring more holes drilled per PCB,” writes Helen Fang, head of Asia Pacific industrials research at HSBC. The increasingly common use of harder laminates is resulting in the bits being consumed more quickly.That’s good news for those making drill bits: HSBC forecasts global demand growing 55% a year in the coming three years. And as with many parts of the AI revolution, the voracious appetite of the sector means that supplies can’t keep up. Even with manufacturers increasing production, the bank forecasts a 24% supply shortfall in PCB drill bits in 2027.That could push the world towards Chinese suppliers, right as the west is trying to wean itself off a dependency on the country for rare earths and other elements necessary to make GPUs. Guangdong Dtech, based in China, is the world’s largest PCB drill bit maker by volume. Around three in every 10 drill bits made in 2025 come from the company, with its monthly capacity potentially climbing from 160 million bits in June to more than 235 million by year-end. Japanese and Taiwanese manufacturers are still dominant at the premium end of the market, according to consultancy Frost & Sullivan, though Chinese manufacturers are trying to close that gap.In its 2026 interim results, Dtech reported that it had begun mass-producing drill bits with aspect ratios exceeding 40:1, while developing techniques for producing bits exceeding 60:1. Its newer diamond-coated tools for particularly tough M9+ board materials have also entered small-scale use.China callingIt’s not just in drill bits that China has a chokehold. Another Chinese manufacturer, Defu Technology, has historically been a key supplier of copper foil for lithium-ion batteries, but is increasingly changing its manufacturing processes to try and capitalise on the AI boom. “AI server PCB/CCL upgrades require smoother HVLP copper foil to reduce high-speed signal loss,” writes Avery Chan, a JP Morgan analyst. What to read next Huawei shelves global AI chip rollout as China's own demand outstrips supply Nvidia cracks down on overseas cloud AI GPU rentals for China Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China HVLP stands for hyper-very-low-profile copper foil, and its manufacturers must make the surface smooth enough to minimise signal loss while making sure it can still stick to the insulating material it is attached to.The business has historically been dominated by suppliers outside mainland China, with Japan’s Mitsui Kinzoku and Furukawa Electric, and Taiwan’s Co-Tech, holding more than 60% of global HVLP supply in 2025. Defu is trying to break in to disrupt that, with the firm shipping around 700 tonnes of HVLP foil in September, including more than 180 tonnes of HVLP4. JP Morgan’s Chan forecasts a shortage of qualified HVLP4 supply of around 700 tonnes a month in 2026, rising to 1,200 tonnes in 2027. Defu plans to add 50,000 tonnes of annual high-end PCB foil capacity over 2027 and 2028. But all the foil it creates will have to get past stringent testing.Testing chipsEven before finished chips reach a server, they must be tested using specialist probe cards and sockets, which themselves rely on sophisticated PCBs of a type not found in a server but just used to check whether the chips work. “PCB is becoming the bottleneck and the value-add in probe cards,” wrote JP Morgan analyst Jerry Tsai.Because of that, China is focusing attention there, too. In September, its Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and National Development and Reform Commission published a five-year plan calling for advances in high-frequency, high-speed and densely layered PCBs, alongside copper-clad laminates, low-profile copper foil and specialist manufacturing equipment.But China won’t see the benefits of building new factories immediately. Producing the most sophisticated PCBs requires experience, specialist equipment and the ability to manufacture complex designs consistently at scale. Tsai warned that “the learning curve is measured in years, rather than quarters.”

items.titleZh: China’s AI hardware push is moving beyond GPUs to the PCBs underneath them — Beijing races to corner the market on copper foil and micro-drill bits as board complexity explodes
items.descriptionZh:
围绕中国AI硬件的关注多集中在国产GPU，尤其是华为昇腾等处理器，因为美国出口限制使先进芯片更难获得。但AI服务器制造远不只是获得处理器：连接芯片、内存和网络设备的印制电路板（PCB）正变得更难生产，中国企业正在竞相供应所需材料和设备。2026年上半年，已有20多家中国PCB制造商宣布大规模扩产计划。汇丰和摩根大通近期报告显示，短缺可能延伸到钻针和铜箔等看似不起眼的环节。汇丰称，用于AI服务器电路板的微型钻针在钻不到200个孔后就可能磨损，而较老材料约为2000个孔，这使制造过程对供应链和制造链各环节都形成压力。

PCB由铜层和绝缘材料层叠而成，再钻孔以连接电路。随着AI服务器处理更多数据，PCB复杂度上升：汇丰估计，笔记本PCB为4至8层，而英伟达H100代GPU超过20层；英伟达Rubin Ultra系统的背板可能包含78层。该行还预测2025至2028年每块板所需孔数年均增长36%。钻孔本身也更困难。台湾凯基证券报告称，孔深与孔径之比已从约20:1升至30:1或40:1，这要求把极细钻针更深地钻入更坚硬材料，同时不能弯曲、断裂或损伤精细电路。新等级覆铜板——铜粘合其上的玻璃纤维和树脂材料——也更难被此前使用的微型碳化钨工具切削。汇丰亚太工业研究主管Helen Fang表示，AI PCB更密集、层数更厚，每块PCB需要钻更多孔；更硬层压板日益普遍，导致钻针消耗更快。

这对钻针制造商是利好：汇丰预测未来三年全球需求每年增长55%；即便制造商增产，2027年PCB钻针仍将短缺24%。这可能使全球更依赖中国供应商，而西方正试图减少对中国稀土等GPU制造所需元素的依赖。总部位于广东的鼎泰高科按产量计是全球最大PCB钻针制造商，2025年每10支钻针中约3支来自该公司，其月产能可能从6月的1.6亿支升至年底超过2.35亿支。Frost & Sullivan称，日本和台湾制造商仍在高端市场占主导，但中国大陆厂商正努力缩小差距。鼎泰高科在2026年中期业绩中报告，已开始量产长径比超过40:1的钻针，并开发超过60:1的生产技术；针对特别坚硬M9+板材的新型金刚石涂层工具也已进入小规模使用。

中国并不只在钻针环节具有卡位优势。另一家中国企业德福科技历史上是锂离子电池铜箔的关键供应商，但正 increasingly 改变制造工艺以抓住AI热潮。摩根大通分析师Avery Chan写道，AI服务器PCB/CCL升级需要更光滑的HVLP铜箔以减少高速信号损耗。HVLP即超低轮廓铜箔，制造商必须让表面足够光滑以最小化信号损耗，同时确保它仍能粘附于绝缘材料。该业务历史上由中国大陆以外供应商主导：2025年日本三井金属、古河电工和台湾Co-Tech占全球HVLP供应超过60%。德福科技正试图切入并打破这一格局，9月出货约700吨HVLP铜箔，其中包括180多吨HVLP4。摩根大通预测2026年合格HVLP4供应每月短缺约700吨，2027年升至1200吨。德福科技计划在2027至2028年新增5万吨/年高端PCB铜箔产能，但所有铜箔都须通过严格测试。

在成品芯片进入服务器前，还必须用专用探针卡和插座测试，而这些部件本身依赖一种不在服务器中使用、仅用于检查芯片是否工作的复杂PCB。摩根大通分析师Jerry Tsai写道，PCB正成为探针卡的瓶颈和增值环节。中国也在关注这一领域：9月，工业和信息化部、国家发展改革委发布五年规划，要求推进高频、高速和密集层压PCB，以及覆铜板、低轮廓铜箔和专用制造设备。但中国不会立即从新工厂获益。生产最复杂PCB需要经验、专用设备以及稳定大规模制造复杂设计的能力。Tsai警告，学习曲线以年而非季度衡量。整体看，AI服务器需求正把PCB及其钻针、铜箔、覆铜板和测试环节推到供应链前台，中国厂商在规模和部分高端产品上加速追赶，但高端材料、设备、良率和客户认证仍是关键门槛。

items.title: Beijing’s AI ambitions are under threat as models may fall behind by up to nine months versus competitors — Chinese AI labs are under heavy fire from export controls, maturing chip stacks and a distillation crackdown
items.description: This week, several reports have detailed how closing GPU rental loopholes across Asia may have had an impact on the development of Chinese AI models.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter This week, several reports have detailed how closing GPU rental loopholes across Asia may have had an impact on the development of Chinese AI models. In September, Mozilla estimated that open-weight AI models were three to six months behind the frontier. Since then, developments in the AI industry and export control rules could mean that Chinese AI models, many of which are typically open-weight, might fall even further behind Western counterparts, by up to nine months.Zhipu AI, the developer of the GLM series of models, has allegedly pushed its release calendar back as a result of reduced access to advanced AI accelerators, Reuters said. It's an open secret that data centers located in Asia have been renting compute capacity to Chinese entities for some time. In light of the recent Nvidia scandal involving Jensen Huang and Megaspeed, the U.S. Department of Commerce has since tightened its rules over how data centers lend their compute capacity to Chinese entities. This has created an environment where there is, in fact, an excess of compute capacity available in the region, Bloomberg reported.These curbs have a knock-on effect on how companies train their AI models, with Nvidia's AI accelerators being the most coveted; not having access to them stifles the development of AI in the region. However, this isn't entirely true across the industry. DeepSeek is attempting to wean itself off foreign silicon and instead adopting Huawei's Ascend AI chips, and porting its libraries away from CUDA and onto the open-source CANN. However, this hasn't stopped Chinese AI labs from facing another issue: tightened security against the distillation of AI models.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Distillation is a practice wherein the way a model thinks can be extracted and then learned from. It is largely believed to be the method in which Chinese AI labs have made great leaps in intelligence over the past several years, though several of China's leading labs refute that claim. The Western frontier has become more obtuse: Anthropic in October detailed how it's leveled up its own defences against distillation attacks, and the obfuscation of an AI model's chain of thought adds another hurdle. According to The Information, this is an issue that DeepSeek is now reportedly reckoning with. If distillation curbs the development of Chinese AI models even further, the gap between Eastern and Western frontier intelligence grows from three to six months to an estimated nine months.The current standingsIf you look at Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, which ranks AI models across a wide range of benchmarks and scores them in numerical order, Anthropic currently has the leading public AI model: Claude Fable 5.2, at a total of 65 points. Meanwhile, the leading Chinese AI model, Kimi K3.1 Pro, sits at 47. Between the two contenders are practically every Western frontier lab: OpenAI, Google, and Meta are all outgunning Chinese competitors, which were, just a few short months ago, competing at the frontier across many tasks. You may like China's open-weight AI models are now just 4 months behind frontier US offerings, Mozilla report claims US frontier AI companies warn authorities over sophisticated distillation attacks Researchers allege DeepSeek, Kimi, and other Chinese AI models were trained using banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs It's important to mention that Artificial Analysis also changed its methodology over recent weeks, with China's AI models falling slightly further behind in added benchmarks, such as the Omniscience score, which tracks how often an AI is likely to hallucinate. This is paired with a jump in capability among the Western labs: Right now, it's on the Chinese AI labs' shoulders to respond in kind, and if current releases are anything to go by, they are falling short of expectations, especially in domains such as cybersecurity. An Epoch AI report characterized the difference in capabilities between GLM 5.3 and Claude Opus 5.5 as a six-to-seven-month gap in intelligence. With the release of newer models like Claude Fable 5.2, it's likely that gap has only widened, and the same story is likely to play out over the next few months across additional domains.With additional safeguards against distillation and powerful compute resources becoming more difficult to find, this poses a difficult question for the Chinese labs: How can they keep up the pace and stay competitive while the odds are stacked against them?China still holds the overall top spot in the open-weight arena with Kimi K3.1 Pro, though Western companies are bringing more performant models out as the months pass. China's second tier of open-weight models, which can often be run locally, e.g Alibaba's Qwen 3.8-27B (20 on AA), is facing competition from the American-made Thinking Machines Labs' Inkling 2 Mini (20 on AA), which was recently released. With the release of the larger (closed-weight and API only) Qwen 4 model seemingly not landing quite as well with users, it remains to be seen whether Alibaba can maintain the advantage of time, as Inkling 2 Mini was released just this week, while Qwen 3.8-27B has been out for several months.With devices like the RTX Spark, AMD's AI Halo, and more, users are increasingly getting their own choice of running an open-weight AI, and for all intents and purposes, that usually means using a Chinese model to get the most intelligence out of your machine. However, recent developments show that smaller Western labs are also beginning to bridge that gap.This is yet another arena in which Chinese and Western labs will want to wrest control from one another. Notably, Google has not released another series of Gemma models following Gemma 4 back in April. If a fifth generation of Google's Gemma models arrives, they'd likely be close cousins to the Gemini Neon, Carbon, Argon, and Hydrogen family, though that remains speculation until Google confirms anything official.The silicon transition Against the backdrop of export controls and tightening restrictions on AI distillation, Chinese AI labs are in a tough spot, and all eyes are on frontier labs like Moonshot AI, Zhipu, Deepseek, Alibaba, and Xiaomi to see if they can scale the intelligence wall that their Western counterparts currently present. More compute for training resources may be an answer, but for comparison's sake, Huawei's upcoming Ascend 950DT accelerator offers 2 PFLOPS of FP4 compute and 1 PFLOPS of FP8, while an Nvidia Rubin R200 offers 50 PFLOPS in inference and 35 PFLOPS in dense workloads. In memory capacity and bandwidth, the Ascend 950DT can offer 144GB of HiZQ 2.0 with 4 TB/s of bandwidth across a 2 TB/s interconnect. Rubin, on the other hand, offers 288GB of HBM4, with bandwidth ranging from 19.2-22 TB/s, across an NvLink interconnect at 2.6 TB/s.If China's AI ambitions are to compete with the West, its silicon needs to either scale so the country can produce more chips to outgun a Western AI deployment with sheer numbers, or it needs to develop more advanced accelerators, while also managing the CANN software stack. The chips are figuratively, and literally, stacked heavily against China. As the race to develop Artificial Intelligence marches on, the Department of Commerce's latest measures have undoubtedly made it incredibly difficult for the country to compete.

items.descriptionZh:
本周多份报道显示，美国通过收紧亚洲地区GPU租赁漏洞，可能已对中国AI模型发展造成实质影响。此前在9月，Mozilla估计开放权重AI模型落后前沿约三到六个月；但此后AI产业变化与出口管制规则收紧，意味着许多通常采用开放权重路线的中国AI模型，可能进一步落后西方对手，差距或扩大至约九个月。路透社称，GLM系列模型开发商智谱AI据称因先进AI加速器获取减少而推迟发布日程。亚洲数据中心长期向中国实体出租算力已是公开的秘密；在涉及英伟达及Megaspeed的风波后，美国商务部收紧了数据中心向中国实体出借算力的规则。彭博社报道称，这反而造成该地区出现算力过剩。限制措施对模型训练产生连锁影响，英伟达AI加速器最受追捧，无法获取会抑制区域AI发展。

不过，行业并非完全一致。DeepSeek正尝试减少对外国芯片的依赖，转而采用华为昇腾AI芯片，并将其库从CUDA迁移至开源CANN。与此同时，中国AI实验室还面临另一问题：针对AI模型蒸馏的安全防护正在加强。蒸馏是指提取模型“思考方式”并加以学习的方法，外界普遍认为中国AI实验室过去几年在智能水平上的跃升主要依赖这一方法，但多家中国领先实验室否认该说法。西方前沿公司正提高防御：Anthropic在10月详细说明如何升级对蒸馏攻击的防御，而对模型思维链的混淆又增加了一道障碍。《The Information》称，DeepSeek如今据报正面对这一问题。如果蒸馏限制进一步遏制中国AI模型发展，东西方前沿智能差距可能从三到六个月扩大至约九个月。

从当前排名看，Artificial Analysis的智能指数按多项基准对AI模型打分排序：Anthropic的Claude Fable 5.2以65分领先，中国领先模型Kimi K3.1 Pro为47分。两者之间几乎排列着所有西方前沿实验室：OpenAI、Google和Meta均领先中国竞争者，而中国模型仅在几个月前还在许多任务上处于前沿竞争。还需注意，Artificial Analysis近几周调整了方法，加入Omniscience评分等新基准，追踪AI产生幻觉的频率，使中国模型略微进一步落后。与此同时，西方实验室能力跃升；目前需要中国AI实验室作出对等回应，而从近期发布看，它们未达预期，尤其在网络安全等领域。Epoch AI报告称，GLM 5.3与Claude Opus 5.5之间的智能差距为六到七个月；随着Claude Fable 5.2等更新模型发布，这一差距可能只会扩大，未来几个月还可能在更多领域重演。

在开放权重领域，中国仍凭Kimi K3.1 Pro占据总体首位，但随着时间推移，西方公司正推出更强模型。中国第二梯队开放权重模型通常可在本地运行，例如阿里巴巴Qwen 3.8-27B在AA上为20分，正面临美国Thinking Machines Labs近期发布的Inkling 2 Mini（同样20分）竞争。更大规模、闭源且仅API提供的Qwen 4似乎未完全获得用户认可，因此阿里巴巴能否保持时间优势仍待观察：Inkling 2 Mini本周才发布，而Qwen 3.8-27B已推出数月。随着RTX Spark、AMD AI Halo等设备普及，用户越来越能自行选择运行开放权重AI，通常意味着使用中国模型以在本地获得最高智能；但近期发展显示，较小规模的西方实验室也开始弥合这一差距。这也是中西实验室争夺控制权的又一战场。值得注意的是，Google自4月发布Gemma 4后尚未推出新的Gemma系列；若第五代Gemma到来，可能与Gemini Neon、Carbon、Argon和Hydrogen家族关系密切，但在Google正式确认前仍属猜测。

在出口管制和AI蒸馏限制收紧背景下，中国AI实验室处境艰难，外界关注Moonshot AI、智谱、DeepSeek、阿里巴巴和小米等前沿实验室能否攀越西方对手当前的智能高墙。增加训练算力可能是答案，但对比来看，华为即将推出的昇腾950DT加速器提供2 PFLOPS FP4算力和1 PFLOPS FP8算力；英伟达Rubin R200则提供50 PFLOPS推理算力和35 PFLOPS密集负载算力。内存容量与带宽方面，昇腾950DT可提供144GB HiZQ 2.0、4 TB/s带宽和2 TB/s互连；Rubin则提供288GB HBM4、19.2-22 TB/s带宽和2.6 TB/s NvLink互连。若中国AI雄心要与西方竞争，其芯片路线要么扩大产能，以数量优势压制西方AI部署，要么开发更先进加速器，同时管理好CANN软件栈。无论比喻还是现实，芯片层面的压力都严重不利于中国；随着AI竞赛推进，美国商务部最新措施无疑使中国竞争变得极其困难。

items.title: TSMC gives a sneap peak at AI Design Kit: Agentic AI with foundry expertise
items.description: TSMC brings agentic AI to chip design as A14 design rule count hits 3.6X that of N5 while customers demand 33% shorter development cycle.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The semiconductor industry is in a paradoxical situation these days. On the one hand, AI drives demand for the leading-edge nodes from both established players and new entrants, with everyone trying to accelerate the development cycle. On the other hand, leading-edge nodes become more complex, which increases entry barriers and stretches design cycles. While the challenge seems to be insoluble, it looks like TSMC has found a solution. (Image credit: TSMC)At its 2026 Europe OIP Ecosystem Workshop in Munich, TSMC this week unveiled its AI Design Kit (ADK), a collection of process-specific technical information, implementation guidelines, and design methodologies that enables AI agents to automate and optimize chip development flows.The ADK complements the foundry's traditional process design kits (PDKs) and enables AI agents to use TSMC's process-specific expertise, knowledge of electronic design automation (EDA) tools, and customers' proprietary design methodologies to automate physical implementation and optimization of chips. Ultimately, the initiative aims to reduce development cycles, improve design productivity, and simplify adoption of TSMC's advanced process technologies.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: "The ADK complements our traditional PDK, and it brings in capabilities to augment the EDA and other design flows," said Aveek Sarkar, Head of Ecosystem and Alliance Management at TSMC. "Our goal with these agentic flows is to bring in the technology-specific learning we have at TSMC and layer that with your orchestration layer, with your design expertise, and to support the next generation of EDA or design flows and methodologies that you have."Why AI?While every new fabrication process from TSMC offers advantages in terms of power, performance, and area (PPA), it also considerably increases design complexity. Compared to TSMC's N5-derived manufacturing technologies (including various N4 nodes), the number of design rules has increased by 2.3X with N3P, 3.1X with N2P, and 3.6X with A14 (the first node to be supported by the ADK). You may like The state of agentic AI in chip design tools in 2026 Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond Cognichip reveals how its new AI-assisted program can slash chip design times from months to days — automating labor-intensive tasks cuts design time down, Chief Product Officer explains Meanwhile, the number of available standard library cells has increased by 2.8X, 5X, and 4.6X, respectively. Add to that a greater number of metallization stack options and plenty of EDA tool settings, and the number of possible design configurations becomes massive. As a result, conventional design optimization methodologies approach their productivity limits, according to TSMC. At the same time, some of TSMC's customers want to reduce their chip development cycles from 18 months to 12 months, Sarkar said. Swipe to scroll horizontally Technology N5/N4P N3P N2P NanoFlex A14 NanoFlex Pro Library HD, HP HD, HP, UHP HD, HP, UHP + Boost Cells HD, HP + Boost Cells Cell Count 1.0x 2.8x 5.0x 4.6x Rule Count 1.0x 2.3x 3.1x 3.6x Usage of agentic AI could help chip developers to explore more design configurations within shorter timeframes, achieve more favorable PPA results from advanced process technologies, and potentially improve manufacturability and yields by implementing more extensive physical design optimization. Furthermore, it could reduce the amount of engineering work required to adopt a new fabrication process for a new design. Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors "AI is bringing a significant benefit: faster design cycles, more verification coverage, faster time to closure," Sarkar said.Do physical implementation fasterTSMC's early-phase AI Design Kit incorporates process-specific information, such as metal pitches, standard cell heights, routing track patterns, library cell naming conventions, and implementation guidelines, according to slides demonstrated at the event. (Image credit: TSMC)With the ADK, EDA agents — such as Cadence's InnoStack or Synopsys's Implementation Agent — can use a simple natural-language prompt and a large language model (LLM) to automatically generate a qualified automatic placement and routing (APR) reference flow for TSMC's A14 process technology. Such a flow includes project setup, library cell usage, placement and routing optimization, routing track and power grid creation, and wide-wire configuration. Traditionally, engineers could spend weeks on preparation of such scripts, but now APR scripts could be prepped with a natural language prompt, though TSMC did not disclose the actual time it takes to prep them (probably because it depends on design complexity and goals). What to read next ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC TSMC's A14 1.4nm-class node is ready for chip design OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design "Instead of spending weeks preparing APR scripts, EDA agents can take a simple prompt from users and the TSMC ADK and use a generative model to deliver a qualified APR reference flow," a spokesperson from TSMC said at the stage.For more sophisticated design tasks, TSMC proposes an orchestration agent that resides at the customer's site and combines three sources of knowledge with clear ownership:Proprietary in-house design know-how, constraints, guidelines, and customized flow;Specialized EDA agents that know how to use EDA tools and their capabilities;TSMC's ADK that provides design reference package and technology-specific information on top of what EDA agent and tools know.The orchestrator coordinates agents responsible for design diagnostics, power grid implementation, timing closure, design rule checks, and congestion mitigation. These agents analyze EDA tool output and automatically adjust parameters for subsequent iterations across floorplanning, placement, clock tree synthesis, routing, sign-off, and engineering change orders (ECOs). Such a methodology enables continuous design optimization 24/7 with less human intervention."The orchestrator then directs these agents to analyze the output of EDA tools and automatically adjust the settings for the next iteration across floorplan, placement, CTS, routing, sign-off, and ECO," the spokesman said. "This agentic AI flow drives the iterative design process 24/7, minimizing the turnaround time and maximizing productivity."Complement, not replaceFor now, TSMC's ADK primarily addresses physical implementation rather than chip architecture or logic design. The company has not demonstrated an autonomous design flow that takes a chip from an architectural specification to tape-out without human intervention. Nor has TSMC disclosed quantified PPA improvements, actual reductions in development cycles, or a commercial availability timeframe for its ADK.It is noteworthy that TSMC's ADK neither replaces conventional PDKs nor substitutes for advanced AI-enabled EDA software from Cadence, Synopsys, Siemens EDA, or other developers. Instead, it provides process-specific knowledge that enables AI agents to make more informed decisions, while the actual physical implementation, simulation, optimization, and verification tasks remain the domain of specialized EDA tools. Thus, chip developers cannot use the ADK independently of traditional EDA infrastructure.Strategic importanceFor TSMC, the ADK could accelerate adoption of its latest fabrication processes, as customers could adapt their design methodologies to new nodes faster. Smaller fabless chip developers could also gain access to sophisticated physical design methodologies without the need to develop expertise comparable to that of prominent chip developers entirely in-house. Meanwhile, EDA and IP providers could benefit from closer integration of their products into process-specific design flows, whereas contract chip designers could offer shorter development times for their customers without significant additional investments.There is also a potential customer lock-in aspect. While TSMC's proposed architecture preserves customers' ownership of proprietary design knowledge, extensive integration of foundry-specific physical design enablement collateral, EDA agents, and internal orchestration systems could make migration to another foundry harder and generally less likely as chipmakers get more accustomed to TSMC ADK (which is an exclusive capability for now and will remain an exclusive offering for a while). In effect, TSMC's competitive advantages will extend well beyond its process technologies, production capabilities, and conventional design ecosystem to include intelligence that emphasizes its customers' chip development methodologies. items.titleZh: 台积电抢先预览AI设计套件：融合晶圆代工专业知识的智能体
items.descriptionZh:
台积电本周在慕尼黑举行的2026年欧洲OIP生态研讨会上发布“AI设计套件”（AI Design Kit，ADK），试图解决先进制程开发中的一个核心矛盾：AI既推动了对尖端节点的强劲需求，又因节点复杂度飙升而拉长设计周期、抬高进入门槛。ADK并非传统工艺设计套件（PDK）的替代品，而是在PDK之外提供工艺特定的技术信息、实施指南和设计方法，使AI代理能够自动化并优化芯片开发流程。其目标是缩短开发周期、提升设计生产率，并降低客户采用台积电先进工艺的难度。

背景方面，台积电每代新工艺虽然在功耗、性能和面积（PPA）上带来优势，但设计复杂度显著上升。与N5/N4P相比，N3P的设计规则数量增加2.3倍，N2P增加3.1倍，A14增加3.6倍；可用标准单元库数量分别增加到2.8倍、5倍和4.6倍。再加上更多金属化堆栈选项和大量EDA工具设置，可能的设计配置数量极其庞大，传统设计优化方法正接近生产率极限。同时，部分客户希望把芯片开发周期从18个月压缩到12个月。台积电生态与联盟管理负责人Aveek Sarkar表示，AI带来的显著好处包括更快的设计周期、更高的验证覆盖率和更快的收敛时间。

ADK的核心创新在于让“代理式AI”进入物理实现环节。早期版本包含金属间距、标准单元高度、布线轨道模式、库单元命名规范和实施指南等工艺特定信息。EDA代理，例如Cadence的InnoStack或Synopsys的Implementation Agent，可以借助自然语言提示和大语言模型，自动生成面向台积电A14工艺的合格自动布局布线（APR）参考流程，涵盖项目设置、库单元使用、布局布线优化、布线轨道与电源网格创建以及宽线配置等。传统上工程师可能需要数周准备这类脚本，而ADK希望用简单提示完成APR参考流程准备，不过台积电未披露实际所需时间，可能取决于设计复杂度和目标。

对于更复杂的设计任务，台积电提出在客户侧部署“编排代理”（orchestration agent），把三类知识结合起来：客户专有的设计诀窍、约束、指南和定制流程；了解EDA工具及其能力的专用EDA代理；以及提供设计参考包和工艺特定信息的台积电ADK。编排代理负责协调设计诊断、电源网格实施、时序收敛、设计规则检查和拥塞缓解等代理。这些代理分析EDA工具输出，并自动调整后续迭代参数，覆盖布局规划、放置、时钟树综合、布线、签核和工程变更订单（ECO），从而支持全天候持续设计优化并减少人工干预。台积电发言人表示，这种代理式AI流程可驱动迭代设计24/7运行，缩短周转时间并最大化生产率。

需要强调的是，ADK目前主要面向物理实现，而非芯片架构或逻辑设计。台积电尚未展示从架构规格到流片全程无需人工干预的自主设计流程，也未披露量化的PPA改善、实际开发周期缩短幅度或ADK商用时间表。ADK既不取代传统PDK，也不替代Cadence、Synopsys、Siemens EDA等公司的AI增强型EDA软件；它提供工艺特定知识，帮助AI代理做出更明智决策，而实际物理实现、仿真、优化和验证仍由专业EDA工具完成。因此，芯片开发商不能脱离传统EDA基础设施单独使用ADK。

从影响看，ADK可能加速客户采用台积电最新工艺，因为客户能更快把设计方法适配到新节点；较小的无晶圆厂芯片公司也可能获得复杂物理设计方法，而不必完全在内部建立与大型芯片开发商相当的专业能力。EDA和IP供应商可通过更紧密地集成到工艺特定设计流程中受益，合同芯片设计公司则可能以较少额外投资为客户提供更短开发时间。与此同时，ADK还存在潜在客户锁定效应：虽然架构保留客户对专有设计知识的所有权，但台积电特定物理设计支持资料、EDA代理和内部编排系统的深度集成，可能使客户迁移到其他晶圆厂更难。ADK目前是台积电独家能力，并将在一段时间内保持独家。由此，台积电的竞争优势可能从工艺技术、产能和传统设计生态，进一步延伸到强调客户芯片开发方法论的“智能”层面。

items.title: Kioxia's 3rd-gen XL-Flash hits Optane-class 3-microsecond read latency with 70% higher density
items.description: Kioxia showed an XL-Flash Generation 3 prototype at KIOXIA Forum in Tokyo and named the upcoming GP2 SSD as its first product.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The Kioxia Corporation showcased a prototype of its new XL-Flash Generation 3 technology, next-generation low-latency, high-performance flash memory, at its KIOXIA Forum in Tokyo. The flash, which uses CMOS directly Bonded to Array, or CBA, for better power efficiency and storage density, is about 135% more efficient with 70% higher bit density than Gen 2, and its 3 µs average read latency is less than 10% of that of Kioxia’s standard BiCS8 TLC. Samples are due March 2027, and Kioxia named its GP2 enterprise SSDs, rated for more than 18 million 512-byte random read IOPS, as its first product using it.The low-latency XL-Flash fills “a new memory tier” to bridge the gap between DRAM and regular flash memory, in a way that can complement or replace some DRAM to help drive down costs, especially in AI servers and data centers. This has some similarities to Optane, which used 3D XPoint instead, as a storage class memory (SCM) option to reach higher IOPS. Intel and Micron’s 3D XPoint stored bits as changes in the cell material’s resistance rather than as trapped charge like NAND, and Intel exited the Optane business in 2022. The XL-Flash NAND is built on BiCS flash technology, but it’s tuned for low read latency and high write endurance. (Image credit: Kioxia)The first generation was SLC with under-5 µs reads, arriving in 2019. By 2022, Gen 2 added 2-bit MLC as an option for lower bit cost, trading some like-for-like performance for better price-to-density. Gen 3 is reported to use SLC, and its 3 µs average read latency challenges the first gen’s sub-5 µs rating while being more than ten times faster than the 40 µs of standard BiCS8 TLC. This is within the same ballpark as Optane SSDs. The flash also reportedly has SLC endurance at 150,000 to 250,000 P/E cycles, at least 50x standard TLC, running at a 4.8 Gb/s interface speed.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Swipe to scroll horizontally Kioxia XL-Flash generations vs. BiCS8 TLC Header Cell - Column 0 Year Cells Die Read latency Gen 1 2019 SLC 128Gb under 5 µs Gen 2 2022 SLC or MLC 128Gb / 256Gb under 5 µs (SLC), under 10 µs (MLC) Gen 3 2026 prototype SLC (reported) 128Gb (reported) 3 µs (average) BiCS8 TLC 2023 TLC 1Tb 40 µs XL-Flash achieves lower latency, in part, by using more, smaller planes (16 per die, with a 4KB page, on earlier generations), which is common with SLC and low-latency flash, and especially helps with smaller I/O. Kioxia’s GP drives target 512B accesses rather than the typical 4KB, a pattern that matches developments in enterprise storage requirements for AI and other emerging workloads that involve constant fine-grained memory lookups. 3D XPoint would outmatch it for write performance, though, due to not needing to erase for new data.The newer gen is able to maintain high levels of performance at much higher density thanks to CBA bonding, where Kioxia makes the logic CMOS wafer and flash memory-cell wafer separately and later bonds them. This technology also improves the efficiency of 512-byte reads, by Kioxia’s own tests, which matches the design intention of the forthcoming GP2. Kioxia hasn’t disclosed full details on the flash, such as layer count. You may like Kioxia unveils E1.L SSDs for hyperscalers with up to 122.88TB capacity Micron's next-generation 3D NAND to double bit density with over 400 layers, offering extreme performance Kioxia Exceria Pro G2 2TB SSD Review — Speed built to last The GP2 Super High IOPS SSD will be Kioxia’s first product to use the new flash, promising high levels of performance, including up to 28 GB/s sequential reads, if it can saturate PCIe 6.0 x4 as expected. Kioxia’s 2.5x IOPS number, versus “typical TLC-based SSDs,” comes from a comparison to its own CM10 drives, for 512B I/O. Endurance will also be excellent at up to 50 drive writes per day, which is within the ballpark of Optane storage.Kioxia is considering E1.S and E3.S form factors, and the drive will support direct liquid cooling, which is increasingly necessary for certain data centers, including GPU-heavy ones where the GP2 is likely to operate. Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware Newsletter Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors These drives will serve as a flash tier to help get more out of a GPU’s HBM, and Kioxia first showed the GP series with Nvidia earlier this year. Offloading memory by any means possible is becoming a strategy with AI, even at the enthusiast level, due to high memory demands and how the technology and its KV caching work. (Image credit: Kioxia)While the flash should sample to select customers before the end of the first quarter of 2027, Kioxia only promises GP2 evaluation samples to select customers by the end of that year. Exact specifications for the drive may differ, but what is clear is that later GP drives will target up to 100 million random-read IOPS that Kioxia and Nvidia have been working toward for AI servers. Kioxia announced its XL1 series of CXL memory expansion modules on XL-Flash in August, and it “will continue to leverage the speed, power efficiency, and endurance of XL-FLASH” for emerging data center needs. items.titleZh: 铠侠第三代XL-Flash实现傲腾级3微秒读取延迟，密度提升70%
items.descriptionZh:
铠侠（Kioxia）在东京KIOXIA Forum上展示了新一代低延迟、高性能闪存XL-Flash Generation 3原型。该产品定位为介于DRAM与普通闪存之间的“新内存层级”，也就是类似存储级内存（SCM）的角色，可在AI服务器和数据中心中补充甚至替代部分DRAM，以降低成本。铠侠称，Gen 3采用CMOS directly Bonded to Array（CBA）技术，把逻辑CMOS晶圆与闪存存储单元晶圆分开制造后再键合，从而提升能效和存储密度；其能效较Gen 2高约135%，位密度高70%，平均读取延迟为3µs，不到铠侠标准BiCS8 TLC的10%。

从技术路线看，XL-Flash仍基于BiCS闪存技术，但针对低读取延迟和高写入耐久进行了调优，与Intel Optane所用的3D XPoint不同。3D XPoint通过存储单元材料电阻变化存储数据，写入时无需像NAND那样先擦除，因此写入性能更强；Intel已于2022年退出Optane业务。XL-Flash则延续NAND路线，通过更多、更小的plane（早期世代为每die 16个plane、4KB页）以及面向小I/O的设计来降低延迟，尤其适合512B这类细粒度访问。铠侠GP系列SSD也针对512B访问而非典型4KB访问，匹配AI等新兴工作负载中频繁的细粒度内存查询需求。

规格对比方面，XL-Flash Gen 1于2019年推出，SLC、128Gb、读取延迟低于5µs；Gen 2于2022年推出，可选SLC或MLC、128Gb/256Gb，SLC低于5µs、MLC低于10µs；Gen 3原型据报道为SLC、128Gb，平均读取延迟3µs。作为对比，2023年的BiCS8 TLC为TLC、1Tb、读取延迟40µs。Gen 3的延迟已接近Optane SSD水平，同时据报道具备SLC级耐久，达15万至25万次P/E循环，至少为标准TLC的50倍，接口速率为4.8Gb/s。CBA键合使新一代在高密度下仍保持高性能，铠侠自测还显示其改善了512B读取效率；不过铠侠尚未披露层数等完整细节。

产品层面，铠侠将GP2企业级SSD列为首款使用XL-Flash Gen 3的产品，额定超过1800万512B随机读取IOPS。GP2预计可通过PCIe 6.0 x4实现最高28GB/s顺序读取；其“2.5倍IOPS”对比的是铠侠自家CM10在512B I/O下的表现，而非所有TLC SSD。耐久最高可达50次全盘写入/天（DWPD），接近Optane存储的水平。GP2考虑E1.S和E3.S形态，并支持直接液冷，以适应GPU密集数据中心的需求。该产品可作为闪存层级，帮助GPU的HBM发挥更大效用；铠侠今年早些时候已与Nvidia联合展示GP系列。AI负载对内存容量和KV缓存要求很高，通过多种方式卸载内存正成为策略。

时间安排上，XL-Flash Gen 3预计2027年3月向部分客户提供样品；GP2评估样品则承诺在2027年底前提供给部分客户。后续GP系列目标是与Nvidia面向AI服务器共同推进至最高1亿随机读取IOPS。铠侠还于今年8月发布了基于XL-Flash的XL1系列CXL内存扩展模块，并表示将继续利用XL-Flash的速度、能效和耐久性满足新兴数据中心需求。

items.title: Texas lifts freeze on 1,800+ data center projects in Greg Abbott U-turn
items.description: After pausing the approval of new data center building permits in August, Texas has now reversed the decision and has once again begun approving applications as builders rush to get the go-ahead before Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa's January arrival.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter After slamming the brakes on more than 1,800 data center projects in August, Texas has once again started approving them following a new directive from outgoing Republican governor Greg Abbott's office. The move came after the same office also paused the approval of permits, saying that Abbot's "top priority is to protect Texans’ safety and quality of life” amid concerns over the amount of power new data centers would require. At the time, the move meant that 474 gigawatts of new power requests became subject to the moratorium. But with Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa's January arrival edging ever closer, Abbott has done a 180-degree pivot, with the FT reporting that data center builders are rushing to get their approvals in before the new governor arrives. Hinojosa has already pledged to rein in new data center construction.As recently as October, Texas suspended a further 17 data center construction permits and shut down an automated portal that was found to still be approving new permits. That system will surely be switched back on now that Abbott's office has confirmed that the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), which is in charge of the state’s electrical grid, has finished gathering the information that it needed on how data centers affect local communities.But even with ERCOT's investigation complete, the processing of new power requests isn't one that is expected to happen quickly. With that in mind, some developers have already taken matters into their own hands, choosing to build their own power centers to reduce or eliminate their reliance on the local grid. The region's large gas supplies are helping this effort, as is what is considered to be a "lax" regulatory environment. This all means that the possibility of using gas turbines to power new data centers is a viable one, although some are looking beyond traditional gas-powered options. In Mississippi, Elon Musk's xAI installed eight converted jet engines to power its data center, despite the known health risks posed by their use.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While it remains to be seen what impact the arrival of incoming Governor Hinojosa will have on data centers in the area, there's little doubt that they will be a hot topic. Locals continue to be concerned about the environmental impact these facilities have, while increased costs associated with powering their own homes are another issue. Texas isn't alone in facing these problems, with New York announcing a year-long ban on data center projects larger than 50 megawatts that came into force earlier this year. In Northern Virginia, Amazon abandoned plans to build four new data centers after public outcry. The land will now be used for housing instead. items.titleZh: 得州解除对1800多个数据中心项目的冻结，格雷格·阿博特态度大转弯
items.descriptionZh:
美国得克萨斯州对数据中心项目的审批政策出现急转。今年8月，即将离任的共和党州长格雷格·阿博特办公室曾叫停1800多个数据中心项目，并暂停相关许可审批，理由是新增数据中心将带来巨大电力需求，而阿博特的“首要任务是保护得州人的安全和生活质量”。当时受影响的新的电力请求规模高达474吉瓦。10月，得州又暂停了17个数据中心建设许可，并关闭了一个仍在自动批准新许可的门户系统。如今，阿博特办公室确认，负责州电网的得州电力可靠性委员会（ERCOT）已完成对数据中心如何影响当地社区的信息收集，得州因此重新开始批准数据中心项目。英国《金融时报》报道称，数据中心建设商正赶在民主党州长吉娜·希诺霍萨明年1月上任前争取获批；希诺霍萨已承诺要遏制新数据中心建设。这意味着审批重启带有明显的政治时间窗口色彩。

从技术和管理层面看，这一事件的核心是AI和云计算数据中心快速扩张带来的电力接入瓶颈。数据中心需要大量稳定电力，审批暂停实际上冻结了巨额新增用电请求。即便ERCOT完成调查，新电力请求的处理预计也不会很快。为此，一些开发商已选择自建发电设施，以减少甚至摆脱对地方电网的依赖。得州丰富的天然气供应和被认为较宽松的监管环境，使燃气轮机为数据中心供电成为可行方案；也有企业探索传统燃气之外的方案。例如，马斯克旗下xAI在密西西比州为其数据中心安装了8台改装喷气发动机供电，尽管这类设备存在已知健康风险。这些做法反映出在电网接入排队和审批不确定性下，现场发电、自备电源正成为数据中心的过渡性或区域性解决方案。

政策影响方面，希诺霍萨上任后对数据中心的态度仍待观察，但数据中心无疑将成为热点议题。当地居民持续担忧数据中心的环境影响，以及居民用电成本上升等问题。得州并非孤例：纽约已实施为期一年的禁令，禁止审批50兆瓦以上的数据中心项目；在北弗吉尼亚，亚马逊因公众反对放弃了四个新数据中心计划，相关土地将改作住房。总体来看，数据中心尤其是AI数据中心的高能耗正从单纯的技术和商业问题，演变为涉及电网可靠性、地方政治、环境负担和居民电费的公共政策问题。得州重新开闸审批，短期内可能让建设商抢在新州长上任前锁定许可，但长期仍面临电网承载力、审批节奏、自备发电环保合规和社区接受度等多重约束。

history.title: China’s AI hardware push is moving beyond GPUs to the PCBs underneath them — Beijing races to corner the market on copper foil and micro-drill bits as board complexity explodes
history.description: AI hardware bottlenecks are expanding beyond GPUs to the PCBs underneath them. As AI servers like Rubin Ultra push PCB layers toward 78 layers using denser laminates, drill bits are wearing out 10 times faster than normal, while high-speed signalling stretches the demand for smooth copper foil.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Much of the attention on China's AI hardware industry has been focused on the country’s drive to develop domestic GPUs, including Huawei's Ascend processors, as U.S. export restrictions make it harder to buy advanced chips in the region. But making an AI server involves far more than securing its processors. The printed circuit boards (PCBs) connecting chips, memory, and networking equipment are becoming harder to manufacture, and Chinese companies are racing to supply the materials and equipment they require.More than 20 Chinese PCB manufacturers announced major expansion plans in the first half of 2026. Three recent reports from HSBC and J.P. Morgan suggest the shortages could extend to products as unglamorous as drill bits and copper foil. Having a plentiful and regular supply of those components in the manufacturing process is important because the tiny drill bit used to make the circuit boards inside AI servers could be worn out after drilling fewer than 200 holes, according to HSBC, compared with around 2,000 holes for older materials.It’s all part of a manufacturing process which stresses every part of the supply and manufacturing chain, beyond obvious components.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: More holes, fewer usesPCBs are built by layering copper and insulating material together, then drilling holes through them to connect their circuits. But the complexity of those boards is increasing as AI servers are designed to handle more data, including more layers than those seen in ordinary computers. HSBC estimates that a notebook PCB has four to eight layers, compared with more than 20 for Nvidia's H100 generation of GPUs.But that’s just the beginning of the process. Analysts at the bank forecast that a backplane in Nvidia’s Rubin Ultra systems could contain 78 layers. Nor is the Rubin Ultra an outlier in that process: the bank also forecasts a 36% annual rise in the number of holes required per board between 2025 and 2028. The holes themselves are becoming more challenging to drill. According to a report by Taiwanese brokerage KGI Securities, the ratio between the depth of the hole and its diameter has increased from around 20:1 to 30:1 or 40:1. That requires pushing an extremely thin drill bit deeper into increasingly tough materials without bending or breaking it, or damaging the delicate circuitry, which can easily happen in such a sophisticated manufacturing process. You may like AI demand triggers massive PCB shortage for PC makers as order books full until 2030 AI component hikes force the world's largest PC makers to return manufacturing capacity to China Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia GPUs in a single year, report claims As well as the number of layers which have to be drilled through increasing in number, the materials involved are also adding complexity to the equation. New grades of copper-clad laminate — the glass-fibre-and-resin material onto which copper is bonded — are becoming trickier for the tiny tungsten-carbide tools previously used in the process to cut. “AI PCBs are denser with thicker layers, requiring more holes drilled per PCB,” writes Helen Fang, head of Asia Pacific industrials research at HSBC. The increasingly common use of harder laminates is resulting in the bits being consumed more quickly.That’s good news for those making drill bits: HSBC forecasts global demand growing 55% a year in the coming three years. And as with many parts of the AI revolution, the voracious appetite of the sector means that supplies can’t keep up. Even with manufacturers increasing production, the bank forecasts a 24% supply shortfall in PCB drill bits in 2027.That could push the world towards Chinese suppliers, right as the west is trying to wean itself off a dependency on the country for rare earths and other elements necessary to make GPUs. Guangdong Dtech, based in China, is the world’s largest PCB drill bit maker by volume. Around three in every 10 drill bits made in 2025 come from the company, with its monthly capacity potentially climbing from 160 million bits in June to more than 235 million by year-end. Japanese and Taiwanese manufacturers are still dominant at the premium end of the market, according to consultancy Frost & Sullivan, though Chinese manufacturers are trying to close that gap.In its 2026 interim results, Dtech reported that it had begun mass-producing drill bits with aspect ratios exceeding 40:1, while developing techniques for producing bits exceeding 60:1. Its newer diamond-coated tools for particularly tough M9+ board materials have also entered small-scale use.China callingIt’s not just in drill bits that China has a chokehold. Another Chinese manufacturer, Defu Technology, has historically been a key supplier of copper foil for lithium-ion batteries, but is increasingly changing its manufacturing processes to try and capitalise on the AI boom. “AI server PCB/CCL upgrades require smoother HVLP copper foil to reduce high-speed signal loss,” writes Avery Chan, a JP Morgan analyst. What to read next Huawei shelves global AI chip rollout as China's own demand outstrips supply Nvidia cracks down on overseas cloud AI GPU rentals for China Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China HVLP stands for hyper-very-low-profile copper foil, and its manufacturers must make the surface smooth enough to minimise signal loss while making sure it can still stick to the insulating material it is attached to.The business has historically been dominated by suppliers outside mainland China, with Japan’s Mitsui Kinzoku and Furukawa Electric, and Taiwan’s Co-Tech, holding more than 60% of global HVLP supply in 2025. Defu is trying to break in to disrupt that, with the firm shipping around 700 tonnes of HVLP foil in September, including more than 180 tonnes of HVLP4. JP Morgan’s Chan forecasts a shortage of qualified HVLP4 supply of around 700 tonnes a month in 2026, rising to 1,200 tonnes in 2027. Defu plans to add 50,000 tonnes of annual high-end PCB foil capacity over 2027 and 2028. But all the foil it creates will have to get past stringent testing.Testing chipsEven before finished chips reach a server, they must be tested using specialist probe cards and sockets, which themselves rely on sophisticated PCBs of a type not found in a server but just used to check whether the chips work. “PCB is becoming the bottleneck and the value-add in probe cards,” wrote JP Morgan analyst Jerry Tsai.Because of that, China is focusing attention there, too. In September, its Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and National Development and Reform Commission published a five-year plan calling for advances in high-frequency, high-speed and densely layered PCBs, alongside copper-clad laminates, low-profile copper foil and specialist manufacturing equipment.But China won’t see the benefits of building new factories immediately. Producing the most sophisticated PCBs requires experience, specialist equipment and the ability to manufacture complex designs consistently at scale. Tsai warned that “the learning curve is measured in years, rather than quarters.”

history.titleZh: China’s AI hardware push is moving beyond GPUs to the PCBs underneath them — Beijing races to corner the market on copper foil and micro-drill bits as board complexity explodes
history.descriptionZh:
围绕中国AI硬件的关注多集中在国产GPU，尤其是华为昇腾等处理器，因为美国出口限制使先进芯片更难获得。但AI服务器制造远不只是获得处理器：连接芯片、内存和网络设备的印制电路板（PCB）正变得更难生产，中国企业正在竞相供应所需材料和设备。2026年上半年，已有20多家中国PCB制造商宣布大规模扩产计划。汇丰和摩根大通近期报告显示，短缺可能延伸到钻针和铜箔等看似不起眼的环节。汇丰称，用于AI服务器电路板的微型钻针在钻不到200个孔后就可能磨损，而较老材料约为2000个孔，这使制造过程对供应链和制造链各环节都形成压力。

PCB由铜层和绝缘材料层叠而成，再钻孔以连接电路。随着AI服务器处理更多数据，PCB复杂度上升：汇丰估计，笔记本PCB为4至8层，而英伟达H100代GPU超过20层；英伟达Rubin Ultra系统的背板可能包含78层。该行还预测2025至2028年每块板所需孔数年均增长36%。钻孔本身也更困难。台湾凯基证券报告称，孔深与孔径之比已从约20:1升至30:1或40:1，这要求把极细钻针更深地钻入更坚硬材料，同时不能弯曲、断裂或损伤精细电路。新等级覆铜板——铜粘合其上的玻璃纤维和树脂材料——也更难被此前使用的微型碳化钨工具切削。汇丰亚太工业研究主管Helen Fang表示，AI PCB更密集、层数更厚，每块PCB需要钻更多孔；更硬层压板日益普遍，导致钻针消耗更快。

这对钻针制造商是利好：汇丰预测未来三年全球需求每年增长55%；即便制造商增产，2027年PCB钻针仍将短缺24%。这可能使全球更依赖中国供应商，而西方正试图减少对中国稀土等GPU制造所需元素的依赖。总部位于广东的鼎泰高科按产量计是全球最大PCB钻针制造商，2025年每10支钻针中约3支来自该公司，其月产能可能从6月的1.6亿支升至年底超过2.35亿支。Frost & Sullivan称，日本和台湾制造商仍在高端市场占主导，但中国大陆厂商正努力缩小差距。鼎泰高科在2026年中期业绩中报告，已开始量产长径比超过40:1的钻针，并开发超过60:1的生产技术；针对特别坚硬M9+板材的新型金刚石涂层工具也已进入小规模使用。

中国并不只在钻针环节具有卡位优势。另一家中国企业德福科技历史上是锂离子电池铜箔的关键供应商，但正 increasingly 改变制造工艺以抓住AI热潮。摩根大通分析师Avery Chan写道，AI服务器PCB/CCL升级需要更光滑的HVLP铜箔以减少高速信号损耗。HVLP即超低轮廓铜箔，制造商必须让表面足够光滑以最小化信号损耗，同时确保它仍能粘附于绝缘材料。该业务历史上由中国大陆以外供应商主导：2025年日本三井金属、古河电工和台湾Co-Tech占全球HVLP供应超过60%。德福科技正试图切入并打破这一格局，9月出货约700吨HVLP铜箔，其中包括180多吨HVLP4。摩根大通预测2026年合格HVLP4供应每月短缺约700吨，2027年升至1200吨。德福科技计划在2027至2028年新增5万吨/年高端PCB铜箔产能，但所有铜箔都须通过严格测试。

在成品芯片进入服务器前，还必须用专用探针卡和插座测试，而这些部件本身依赖一种不在服务器中使用、仅用于检查芯片是否工作的复杂PCB。摩根大通分析师Jerry Tsai写道，PCB正成为探针卡的瓶颈和增值环节。中国也在关注这一领域：9月，工业和信息化部、国家发展改革委发布五年规划，要求推进高频、高速和密集层压PCB，以及覆铜板、低轮廓铜箔和专用制造设备。但中国不会立即从新工厂获益。生产最复杂PCB需要经验、专用设备以及稳定大规模制造复杂设计的能力。Tsai警告，学习曲线以年而非季度衡量。整体看，AI服务器需求正把PCB及其钻针、铜箔、覆铜板和测试环节推到供应链前台，中国厂商在规模和部分高端产品上加速追赶，但高端材料、设备、良率和客户认证仍是关键门槛。

history.title: Beijing’s AI ambitions are under threat as models may fall behind by up to nine months versus competitors — Chinese AI labs are under heavy fire from export controls, maturing chip stacks and a distillation crackdown
history.description: This week, several reports have detailed how closing GPU rental loopholes across Asia may have had an impact on the development of Chinese AI models.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter This week, several reports have detailed how closing GPU rental loopholes across Asia may have had an impact on the development of Chinese AI models. In September, Mozilla estimated that open-weight AI models were three to six months behind the frontier. Since then, developments in the AI industry and export control rules could mean that Chinese AI models, many of which are typically open-weight, might fall even further behind Western counterparts, by up to nine months.Zhipu AI, the developer of the GLM series of models, has allegedly pushed its release calendar back as a result of reduced access to advanced AI accelerators, Reuters said. It's an open secret that data centers located in Asia have been renting compute capacity to Chinese entities for some time. In light of the recent Nvidia scandal involving Jensen Huang and Megaspeed, the U.S. Department of Commerce has since tightened its rules over how data centers lend their compute capacity to Chinese entities. This has created an environment where there is, in fact, an excess of compute capacity available in the region, Bloomberg reported.These curbs have a knock-on effect on how companies train their AI models, with Nvidia's AI accelerators being the most coveted; not having access to them stifles the development of AI in the region. However, this isn't entirely true across the industry. DeepSeek is attempting to wean itself off foreign silicon and instead adopting Huawei's Ascend AI chips, and porting its libraries away from CUDA and onto the open-source CANN. However, this hasn't stopped Chinese AI labs from facing another issue: tightened security against the distillation of AI models.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Distillation is a practice wherein the way a model thinks can be extracted and then learned from. It is largely believed to be the method in which Chinese AI labs have made great leaps in intelligence over the past several years, though several of China's leading labs refute that claim. The Western frontier has become more obtuse: Anthropic in October detailed how it's leveled up its own defences against distillation attacks, and the obfuscation of an AI model's chain of thought adds another hurdle. According to The Information, this is an issue that DeepSeek is now reportedly reckoning with. If distillation curbs the development of Chinese AI models even further, the gap between Eastern and Western frontier intelligence grows from three to six months to an estimated nine months.The current standingsIf you look at Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, which ranks AI models across a wide range of benchmarks and scores them in numerical order, Anthropic currently has the leading public AI model: Claude Fable 5.2, at a total of 65 points. Meanwhile, the leading Chinese AI model, Kimi K3.1 Pro, sits at 47. Between the two contenders are practically every Western frontier lab: OpenAI, Google, and Meta are all outgunning Chinese competitors, which were, just a few short months ago, competing at the frontier across many tasks. You may like China's open-weight AI models are now just 4 months behind frontier US offerings, Mozilla report claims US frontier AI companies warn authorities over sophisticated distillation attacks Researchers allege DeepSeek, Kimi, and other Chinese AI models were trained using banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs It's important to mention that Artificial Analysis also changed its methodology over recent weeks, with China's AI models falling slightly further behind in added benchmarks, such as the Omniscience score, which tracks how often an AI is likely to hallucinate. This is paired with a jump in capability among the Western labs: Right now, it's on the Chinese AI labs' shoulders to respond in kind, and if current releases are anything to go by, they are falling short of expectations, especially in domains such as cybersecurity. An Epoch AI report characterized the difference in capabilities between GLM 5.3 and Claude Opus 5.5 as a six-to-seven-month gap in intelligence. With the release of newer models like Claude Fable 5.2, it's likely that gap has only widened, and the same story is likely to play out over the next few months across additional domains.With additional safeguards against distillation and powerful compute resources becoming more difficult to find, this poses a difficult question for the Chinese labs: How can they keep up the pace and stay competitive while the odds are stacked against them?China still holds the overall top spot in the open-weight arena with Kimi K3.1 Pro, though Western companies are bringing more performant models out as the months pass. China's second tier of open-weight models, which can often be run locally, e.g Alibaba's Qwen 3.8-27B (20 on AA), is facing competition from the American-made Thinking Machines Labs' Inkling 2 Mini (20 on AA), which was recently released. With the release of the larger (closed-weight and API only) Qwen 4 model seemingly not landing quite as well with users, it remains to be seen whether Alibaba can maintain the advantage of time, as Inkling 2 Mini was released just this week, while Qwen 3.8-27B has been out for several months.With devices like the RTX Spark, AMD's AI Halo, and more, users are increasingly getting their own choice of running an open-weight AI, and for all intents and purposes, that usually means using a Chinese model to get the most intelligence out of your machine. However, recent developments show that smaller Western labs are also beginning to bridge that gap.This is yet another arena in which Chinese and Western labs will want to wrest control from one another. Notably, Google has not released another series of Gemma models following Gemma 4 back in April. If a fifth generation of Google's Gemma models arrives, they'd likely be close cousins to the Gemini Neon, Carbon, Argon, and Hydrogen family, though that remains speculation until Google confirms anything official.The silicon transition Against the backdrop of export controls and tightening restrictions on AI distillation, Chinese AI labs are in a tough spot, and all eyes are on frontier labs like Moonshot AI, Zhipu, Deepseek, Alibaba, and Xiaomi to see if they can scale the intelligence wall that their Western counterparts currently present. More compute for training resources may be an answer, but for comparison's sake, Huawei's upcoming Ascend 950DT accelerator offers 2 PFLOPS of FP4 compute and 1 PFLOPS of FP8, while an Nvidia Rubin R200 offers 50 PFLOPS in inference and 35 PFLOPS in dense workloads. In memory capacity and bandwidth, the Ascend 950DT can offer 144GB of HiZQ 2.0 with 4 TB/s of bandwidth across a 2 TB/s interconnect. Rubin, on the other hand, offers 288GB of HBM4, with bandwidth ranging from 19.2-22 TB/s, across an NvLink interconnect at 2.6 TB/s.If China's AI ambitions are to compete with the West, its silicon needs to either scale so the country can produce more chips to outgun a Western AI deployment with sheer numbers, or it needs to develop more advanced accelerators, while also managing the CANN software stack. The chips are figuratively, and literally, stacked heavily against China. As the race to develop Artificial Intelligence marches on, the Department of Commerce's latest measures have undoubtedly made it incredibly difficult for the country to compete.

history.titleZh: Beijing’s AI ambitions are under threat as models may fall behind by up to nine months versus competitors — Chinese AI labs are under heavy fire from export controls, maturing chip stacks and a distillation crackdown
history.descriptionZh:
本周多份报道显示，美国通过收紧亚洲地区GPU租赁漏洞，可能已对中国AI模型发展造成实质影响。此前在9月，Mozilla估计开放权重AI模型落后前沿约三到六个月；但此后AI产业变化与出口管制规则收紧，意味着许多通常采用开放权重路线的中国AI模型，可能进一步落后西方对手，差距或扩大至约九个月。路透社称，GLM系列模型开发商智谱AI据称因先进AI加速器获取减少而推迟发布日程。亚洲数据中心长期向中国实体出租算力已是公开的秘密；在涉及英伟达及Megaspeed的风波后，美国商务部收紧了数据中心向中国实体出借算力的规则。彭博社报道称，这反而造成该地区出现算力过剩。限制措施对模型训练产生连锁影响，英伟达AI加速器最受追捧，无法获取会抑制区域AI发展。

不过，行业并非完全一致。DeepSeek正尝试减少对外国芯片的依赖，转而采用华为昇腾AI芯片，并将其库从CUDA迁移至开源CANN。与此同时，中国AI实验室还面临另一问题：针对AI模型蒸馏的安全防护正在加强。蒸馏是指提取模型“思考方式”并加以学习的方法，外界普遍认为中国AI实验室过去几年在智能水平上的跃升主要依赖这一方法，但多家中国领先实验室否认该说法。西方前沿公司正提高防御：Anthropic在10月详细说明如何升级对蒸馏攻击的防御，而对模型思维链的混淆又增加了一道障碍。《The Information》称，DeepSeek如今据报正面对这一问题。如果蒸馏限制进一步遏制中国AI模型发展，东西方前沿智能差距可能从三到六个月扩大至约九个月。

从当前排名看，Artificial Analysis的智能指数按多项基准对AI模型打分排序：Anthropic的Claude Fable 5.2以65分领先，中国领先模型Kimi K3.1 Pro为47分。两者之间几乎排列着所有西方前沿实验室：OpenAI、Google和Meta均领先中国竞争者，而中国模型仅在几个月前还在许多任务上处于前沿竞争。还需注意，Artificial Analysis近几周调整了方法，加入Omniscience评分等新基准，追踪AI产生幻觉的频率，使中国模型略微进一步落后。与此同时，西方实验室能力跃升；目前需要中国AI实验室作出对等回应，而从近期发布看，它们未达预期，尤其在网络安全等领域。Epoch AI报告称，GLM 5.3与Claude Opus 5.5之间的智能差距为六到七个月；随着Claude Fable 5.2等更新模型发布，这一差距可能只会扩大，未来几个月还可能在更多领域重演。

在开放权重领域，中国仍凭Kimi K3.1 Pro占据总体首位，但随着时间推移，西方公司正推出更强模型。中国第二梯队开放权重模型通常可在本地运行，例如阿里巴巴Qwen 3.8-27B在AA上为20分，正面临美国Thinking Machines Labs近期发布的Inkling 2 Mini（同样20分）竞争。更大规模、闭源且仅API提供的Qwen 4似乎未完全获得用户认可，因此阿里巴巴能否保持时间优势仍待观察：Inkling 2 Mini本周才发布，而Qwen 3.8-27B已推出数月。随着RTX Spark、AMD AI Halo等设备普及，用户越来越能自行选择运行开放权重AI，通常意味着使用中国模型以在本地获得最高智能；但近期发展显示，较小规模的西方实验室也开始弥合这一差距。这也是中西实验室争夺控制权的又一战场。值得注意的是，Google自4月发布Gemma 4后尚未推出新的Gemma系列；若第五代Gemma到来，可能与Gemini Neon、Carbon、Argon和Hydrogen家族关系密切，但在Google正式确认前仍属猜测。

在出口管制和AI蒸馏限制收紧背景下，中国AI实验室处境艰难，外界关注Moonshot AI、智谱、DeepSeek、阿里巴巴和小米等前沿实验室能否攀越西方对手当前的智能高墙。增加训练算力可能是答案，但对比来看，华为即将推出的昇腾950DT加速器提供2 PFLOPS FP4算力和1 PFLOPS FP8算力；英伟达Rubin R200则提供50 PFLOPS推理算力和35 PFLOPS密集负载算力。内存容量与带宽方面，昇腾950DT可提供144GB HiZQ 2.0、4 TB/s带宽和2 TB/s互连；Rubin则提供288GB HBM4、19.2-22 TB/s带宽和2.6 TB/s NvLink互连。若中国AI雄心要与西方竞争，其芯片路线要么扩大产能，以数量优势压制西方AI部署，要么开发更先进加速器，同时管理好CANN软件栈。无论比喻还是现实，芯片层面的压力都严重不利于中国；随着AI竞赛推进，美国商务部最新措施无疑使中国竞争变得极其困难。

history.title: TSMC gives a sneap peak at AI Design Kit: Agentic AI with foundry expertise
history.description: TSMC brings agentic AI to chip design as A14 design rule count hits 3.6X that of N5 while customers demand 33% shorter development cycle.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The semiconductor industry is in a paradoxical situation these days. On the one hand, AI drives demand for the leading-edge nodes from both established players and new entrants, with everyone trying to accelerate the development cycle. On the other hand, leading-edge nodes become more complex, which increases entry barriers and stretches design cycles. While the challenge seems to be insoluble, it looks like TSMC has found a solution. (Image credit: TSMC)At its 2026 Europe OIP Ecosystem Workshop in Munich, TSMC this week unveiled its AI Design Kit (ADK), a collection of process-specific technical information, implementation guidelines, and design methodologies that enables AI agents to automate and optimize chip development flows.The ADK complements the foundry's traditional process design kits (PDKs) and enables AI agents to use TSMC's process-specific expertise, knowledge of electronic design automation (EDA) tools, and customers' proprietary design methodologies to automate physical implementation and optimization of chips. Ultimately, the initiative aims to reduce development cycles, improve design productivity, and simplify adoption of TSMC's advanced process technologies.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: "The ADK complements our traditional PDK, and it brings in capabilities to augment the EDA and other design flows," said Aveek Sarkar, Head of Ecosystem and Alliance Management at TSMC. "Our goal with these agentic flows is to bring in the technology-specific learning we have at TSMC and layer that with your orchestration layer, with your design expertise, and to support the next generation of EDA or design flows and methodologies that you have."Why AI?While every new fabrication process from TSMC offers advantages in terms of power, performance, and area (PPA), it also considerably increases design complexity. Compared to TSMC's N5-derived manufacturing technologies (including various N4 nodes), the number of design rules has increased by 2.3X with N3P, 3.1X with N2P, and 3.6X with A14 (the first node to be supported by the ADK). You may like The state of agentic AI in chip design tools in 2026 Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond Cognichip reveals how its new AI-assisted program can slash chip design times from months to days — automating labor-intensive tasks cuts design time down, Chief Product Officer explains Meanwhile, the number of available standard library cells has increased by 2.8X, 5X, and 4.6X, respectively. Add to that a greater number of metallization stack options and plenty of EDA tool settings, and the number of possible design configurations becomes massive. As a result, conventional design optimization methodologies approach their productivity limits, according to TSMC. At the same time, some of TSMC's customers want to reduce their chip development cycles from 18 months to 12 months, Sarkar said. Swipe to scroll horizontally Technology N5/N4P N3P N2P NanoFlex A14 NanoFlex Pro Library HD, HP HD, HP, UHP HD, HP, UHP + Boost Cells HD, HP + Boost Cells Cell Count 1.0x 2.8x 5.0x 4.6x Rule Count 1.0x 2.3x 3.1x 3.6x Usage of agentic AI could help chip developers to explore more design configurations within shorter timeframes, achieve more favorable PPA results from advanced process technologies, and potentially improve manufacturability and yields by implementing more extensive physical design optimization. Furthermore, it could reduce the amount of engineering work required to adopt a new fabrication process for a new design. Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware Newsletter Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors "AI is bringing a significant benefit: faster design cycles, more verification coverage, faster time to closure," Sarkar said.Do physical implementation fasterTSMC's early-phase AI Design Kit incorporates process-specific information, such as metal pitches, standard cell heights, routing track patterns, library cell naming conventions, and implementation guidelines, according to slides demonstrated at the event. (Image credit: TSMC)With the ADK, EDA agents — such as Cadence's InnoStack or Synopsys's Implementation Agent — can use a simple natural-language prompt and a large language model (LLM) to automatically generate a qualified automatic placement and routing (APR) reference flow for TSMC's A14 process technology. Such a flow includes project setup, library cell usage, placement and routing optimization, routing track and power grid creation, and wide-wire configuration. Traditionally, engineers could spend weeks on preparation of such scripts, but now APR scripts could be prepped with a natural language prompt, though TSMC did not disclose the actual time it takes to prep them (probably because it depends on design complexity and goals). What to read next ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC TSMC's A14 1.4nm-class node is ready for chip design OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design "Instead of spending weeks preparing APR scripts, EDA agents can take a simple prompt from users and the TSMC ADK and use a generative model to deliver a qualified APR reference flow," a spokesperson from TSMC said at the stage.For more sophisticated design tasks, TSMC proposes an orchestration agent that resides at the customer's site and combines three sources of knowledge with clear ownership:Proprietary in-house design know-how, constraints, guidelines, and customized flow;Specialized EDA agents that know how to use EDA tools and their capabilities;TSMC's ADK that provides design reference package and technology-specific information on top of what EDA agent and tools know.The orchestrator coordinates agents responsible for design diagnostics, power grid implementation, timing closure, design rule checks, and congestion mitigation. These agents analyze EDA tool output and automatically adjust parameters for subsequent iterations across floorplanning, placement, clock tree synthesis, routing, sign-off, and engineering change orders (ECOs). Such a methodology enables continuous design optimization 24/7 with less human intervention."The orchestrator then directs these agents to analyze the output of EDA tools and automatically adjust the settings for the next iteration across floorplan, placement, CTS, routing, sign-off, and ECO," the spokesman said. "This agentic AI flow drives the iterative design process 24/7, minimizing the turnaround time and maximizing productivity."Complement, not replaceFor now, TSMC's ADK primarily addresses physical implementation rather than chip architecture or logic design. The company has not demonstrated an autonomous design flow that takes a chip from an architectural specification to tape-out without human intervention. Nor has TSMC disclosed quantified PPA improvements, actual reductions in development cycles, or a commercial availability timeframe for its ADK.It is noteworthy that TSMC's ADK neither replaces conventional PDKs nor substitutes for advanced AI-enabled EDA software from Cadence, Synopsys, Siemens EDA, or other developers. Instead, it provides process-specific knowledge that enables AI agents to make more informed decisions, while the actual physical implementation, simulation, optimization, and verification tasks remain the domain of specialized EDA tools. Thus, chip developers cannot use the ADK independently of traditional EDA infrastructure.Strategic importanceFor TSMC, the ADK could accelerate adoption of its latest fabrication processes, as customers could adapt their design methodologies to new nodes faster. Smaller fabless chip developers could also gain access to sophisticated physical design methodologies without the need to develop expertise comparable to that of prominent chip developers entirely in-house. Meanwhile, EDA and IP providers could benefit from closer integration of their products into process-specific design flows, whereas contract chip designers could offer shorter development times for their customers without significant additional investments.There is also a potential customer lock-in aspect. While TSMC's proposed architecture preserves customers' ownership of proprietary design knowledge, extensive integration of foundry-specific physical design enablement collateral, EDA agents, and internal orchestration systems could make migration to another foundry harder and generally less likely as chipmakers get more accustomed to TSMC ADK (which is an exclusive capability for now and will remain an exclusive offering for a while). In effect, TSMC's competitive advantages will extend well beyond its process technologies, production capabilities, and conventional design ecosystem to include intelligence that emphasizes its customers' chip development methodologies. history.titleZh: 台积电抢先预览AI设计套件：融合晶圆代工专业知识的智能体
history.descriptionZh:
台积电本周在慕尼黑举行的2026年欧洲OIP生态研讨会上发布“AI设计套件”（AI Design Kit，ADK），试图解决先进制程开发中的一个核心矛盾：AI既推动了对尖端节点的强劲需求，又因节点复杂度飙升而拉长设计周期、抬高进入门槛。ADK并非传统工艺设计套件（PDK）的替代品，而是在PDK之外提供工艺特定的技术信息、实施指南和设计方法，使AI代理能够自动化并优化芯片开发流程。其目标是缩短开发周期、提升设计生产率，并降低客户采用台积电先进工艺的难度。

背景方面，台积电每代新工艺虽然在功耗、性能和面积（PPA）上带来优势，但设计复杂度显著上升。与N5/N4P相比，N3P的设计规则数量增加2.3倍，N2P增加3.1倍，A14增加3.6倍；可用标准单元库数量分别增加到2.8倍、5倍和4.6倍。再加上更多金属化堆栈选项和大量EDA工具设置，可能的设计配置数量极其庞大，传统设计优化方法正接近生产率极限。同时，部分客户希望把芯片开发周期从18个月压缩到12个月。台积电生态与联盟管理负责人Aveek Sarkar表示，AI带来的显著好处包括更快的设计周期、更高的验证覆盖率和更快的收敛时间。

ADK的核心创新在于让“代理式AI”进入物理实现环节。早期版本包含金属间距、标准单元高度、布线轨道模式、库单元命名规范和实施指南等工艺特定信息。EDA代理，例如Cadence的InnoStack或Synopsys的Implementation Agent，可以借助自然语言提示和大语言模型，自动生成面向台积电A14工艺的合格自动布局布线（APR）参考流程，涵盖项目设置、库单元使用、布局布线优化、布线轨道与电源网格创建以及宽线配置等。传统上工程师可能需要数周准备这类脚本，而ADK希望用简单提示完成APR参考流程准备，不过台积电未披露实际所需时间，可能取决于设计复杂度和目标。

对于更复杂的设计任务，台积电提出在客户侧部署“编排代理”（orchestration agent），把三类知识结合起来：客户专有的设计诀窍、约束、指南和定制流程；了解EDA工具及其能力的专用EDA代理；以及提供设计参考包和工艺特定信息的台积电ADK。编排代理负责协调设计诊断、电源网格实施、时序收敛、设计规则检查和拥塞缓解等代理。这些代理分析EDA工具输出，并自动调整后续迭代参数，覆盖布局规划、放置、时钟树综合、布线、签核和工程变更订单（ECO），从而支持全天候持续设计优化并减少人工干预。台积电发言人表示，这种代理式AI流程可驱动迭代设计24/7运行，缩短周转时间并最大化生产率。

需要强调的是，ADK目前主要面向物理实现，而非芯片架构或逻辑设计。台积电尚未展示从架构规格到流片全程无需人工干预的自主设计流程，也未披露量化的PPA改善、实际开发周期缩短幅度或ADK商用时间表。ADK既不取代传统PDK，也不替代Cadence、Synopsys、Siemens EDA等公司的AI增强型EDA软件；它提供工艺特定知识，帮助AI代理做出更明智决策，而实际物理实现、仿真、优化和验证仍由专业EDA工具完成。因此，芯片开发商不能脱离传统EDA基础设施单独使用ADK。

从影响看，ADK可能加速客户采用台积电最新工艺，因为客户能更快把设计方法适配到新节点；较小的无晶圆厂芯片公司也可能获得复杂物理设计方法，而不必完全在内部建立与大型芯片开发商相当的专业能力。EDA和IP供应商可通过更紧密地集成到工艺特定设计流程中受益，合同芯片设计公司则可能以较少额外投资为客户提供更短开发时间。与此同时，ADK还存在潜在客户锁定效应：虽然架构保留客户对专有设计知识的所有权，但台积电特定物理设计支持资料、EDA代理和内部编排系统的深度集成，可能使客户迁移到其他晶圆厂更难。ADK目前是台积电独家能力，并将在一段时间内保持独家。由此，台积电的竞争优势可能从工艺技术、产能和传统设计生态，进一步延伸到强调客户芯片开发方法论的“智能”层面。

history.title: Kioxia's 3rd-gen XL-Flash hits Optane-class 3-microsecond read latency with 70% higher density
history.description: Kioxia showed an XL-Flash Generation 3 prototype at KIOXIA Forum in Tokyo and named the upcoming GP2 SSD as its first product.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The Kioxia Corporation showcased a prototype of its new XL-Flash Generation 3 technology, next-generation low-latency, high-performance flash memory, at its KIOXIA Forum in Tokyo. The flash, which uses CMOS directly Bonded to Array, or CBA, for better power efficiency and storage density, is about 135% more efficient with 70% higher bit density than Gen 2, and its 3 µs average read latency is less than 10% of that of Kioxia’s standard BiCS8 TLC. Samples are due March 2027, and Kioxia named its GP2 enterprise SSDs, rated for more than 18 million 512-byte random read IOPS, as its first product using it.The low-latency XL-Flash fills “a new memory tier” to bridge the gap between DRAM and regular flash memory, in a way that can complement or replace some DRAM to help drive down costs, especially in AI servers and data centers. This has some similarities to Optane, which used 3D XPoint instead, as a storage class memory (SCM) option to reach higher IOPS. Intel and Micron’s 3D XPoint stored bits as changes in the cell material’s resistance rather than as trapped charge like NAND, and Intel exited the Optane business in 2022. The XL-Flash NAND is built on BiCS flash technology, but it’s tuned for low read latency and high write endurance. (Image credit: Kioxia)The first generation was SLC with under-5 µs reads, arriving in 2019. By 2022, Gen 2 added 2-bit MLC as an option for lower bit cost, trading some like-for-like performance for better price-to-density. Gen 3 is reported to use SLC, and its 3 µs average read latency challenges the first gen’s sub-5 µs rating while being more than ten times faster than the 40 µs of standard BiCS8 TLC. This is within the same ballpark as Optane SSDs. The flash also reportedly has SLC endurance at 150,000 to 250,000 P/E cycles, at least 50x standard TLC, running at a 4.8 Gb/s interface speed.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Swipe to scroll horizontally Kioxia XL-Flash generations vs. BiCS8 TLC Header Cell - Column 0 Year Cells Die Read latency Gen 1 2019 SLC 128Gb under 5 µs Gen 2 2022 SLC or MLC 128Gb / 256Gb under 5 µs (SLC), under 10 µs (MLC) Gen 3 2026 prototype SLC (reported) 128Gb (reported) 3 µs (average) BiCS8 TLC 2023 TLC 1Tb 40 µs XL-Flash achieves lower latency, in part, by using more, smaller planes (16 per die, with a 4KB page, on earlier generations), which is common with SLC and low-latency flash, and especially helps with smaller I/O. Kioxia’s GP drives target 512B accesses rather than the typical 4KB, a pattern that matches developments in enterprise storage requirements for AI and other emerging workloads that involve constant fine-grained memory lookups. 3D XPoint would outmatch it for write performance, though, due to not needing to erase for new data.The newer gen is able to maintain high levels of performance at much higher density thanks to CBA bonding, where Kioxia makes the logic CMOS wafer and flash memory-cell wafer separately and later bonds them. This technology also improves the efficiency of 512-byte reads, by Kioxia’s own tests, which matches the design intention of the forthcoming GP2. Kioxia hasn’t disclosed full details on the flash, such as layer count. You may like Kioxia unveils E1.L SSDs for hyperscalers with up to 122.88TB capacity Micron's next-generation 3D NAND to double bit density with over 400 layers, offering extreme performance Kioxia Exceria Pro G2 2TB SSD Review — Speed built to last The GP2 Super High IOPS SSD will be Kioxia’s first product to use the new flash, promising high levels of performance, including up to 28 GB/s sequential reads, if it can saturate PCIe 6.0 x4 as expected. Kioxia’s 2.5x IOPS number, versus “typical TLC-based SSDs,” comes from a comparison to its own CM10 drives, for 512B I/O. Endurance will also be excellent at up to 50 drive writes per day, which is within the ballpark of Optane storage.Kioxia is considering E1.S and E3.S form factors, and the drive will support direct liquid cooling, which is increasingly necessary for certain data centers, including GPU-heavy ones where the GP2 is likely to operate. Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware Newsletter Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors These drives will serve as a flash tier to help get more out of a GPU’s HBM, and Kioxia first showed the GP series with Nvidia earlier this year. Offloading memory by any means possible is becoming a strategy with AI, even at the enthusiast level, due to high memory demands and how the technology and its KV caching work. (Image credit: Kioxia)While the flash should sample to select customers before the end of the first quarter of 2027, Kioxia only promises GP2 evaluation samples to select customers by the end of that year. Exact specifications for the drive may differ, but what is clear is that later GP drives will target up to 100 million random-read IOPS that Kioxia and Nvidia have been working toward for AI servers. Kioxia announced its XL1 series of CXL memory expansion modules on XL-Flash in August, and it “will continue to leverage the speed, power efficiency, and endurance of XL-FLASH” for emerging data center needs.
